readings: done is asserted combinationally in the same clock cycle in which the stop bit is sampled (e.g., done = (state == STOP && in == 1)).
done is registered and asserted in the clock cycle after the stop bit is sampled (e.g., set in a DONE state on the next clock edge).
When the stop bit is 0, the FSM enters a wait state and does not assert done or update out_byte; upon seeing a 1, it returns to idle to look for the next start bit.
When the stop bit is 0, the FSM enters a wait state; when it sees a 1, it asserts done and outputs the previously received data byte (treating the 1 as a found stop bit).
Synchronous reset only affects the state at the clock edge; done and out_byte retain their previous values during the cycle reset is high, and are cleared on the next clock edge.
Reset forces done=0 and out_byte=0 combinationally during the same cycle reset is high, even though the spec says synchronous.
